title: This Shark Walks on Land and Survives 2 Hours With No Oxygen

scenes.text: A shark that walks out of the sea. On its fins.
The epaulette shark, about three feet long, from the reefs of northern Australia and New Guinea.
At low tide its pool runs out of oxygen. Most fish would be dead in minutes.
This one shrugs it off. Roughly two hours with no oxygen at all.
Then it walks. Paddle-shaped fins, about ninety feet over bare rock, to the next pool.
Researchers call it the toughest shark on the Great Barrier Reef. Not the biggest. The one that walks away.

description:
The epaulette shark can walk on land with its paddle-shaped fins and survive about two hours with no oxygen at all.
It lives in shallow reef pools around northern Australia and New Guinea that lose their oxygen at low tide, so it crawls roughly 90 feet across exposed rock to the next pool. Researchers at Florida Atlantic University and James Cook University call it the toughest shark on the Great Barrier Reef.
What other animal would you call the toughest in its habitat?

first_comment: Newborn epaulette sharks can already walk, living off a yolk sac for their first month. Which animal do you think is the toughest survivor on Earth?
